task.description: ELIXIR-DEV (WF-02 Step 2a) for REQ-159. Implement lib/letflow/design/req159-lua-host-api-read.md, which passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR after 1 rework round (a genuine security-relevant fix: get_instance_state restricted to a script's own instance only, no cross-instance reads even within the same tenant -- read section 5 carefully, this restriction is load-bearing, not incidental). Read the design in full before starting. Build: (1) new lib/letflow/engine/lua_number_marshalling.ex -- Letflow.Engine.LuaNumberMarshalling per REQ-150 Section 3 exactly: to_lua/1 and from_lua/1, both identity functions for integer/float/nil (and pass-through for other term() shapes, per that design's own scope statement -- do not invent behavior for strings/booleans/maps/lists beyond identity, since REQ-150 explicitly left those out of scope but the signatures must accept term()). (2) Extend lib/letflow/engine/lua/platform.ex: add an execution_context parameter (per the design's exact shape: %{instance_id, prefix, trace_id, script_identity, variables}) threaded through a new install/3, with install/1 and install/2 staying source-compatible by delegating to install/3 with an empty execution-context sentinel (per the design's exact specification -- read it precisely, do not improvise the sentinel's shape). Replace exactly 3 of the 6 gated stub_funs -- read_variable, get_instance_state, log -- with real implementations per the design's sections 4/5/6. Do NOT touch write_variable, call_service, emit_event (REQ-160's), or now/fail, and do NOT change any required_capability_fun (only stub_fun changes for these 3 rows). read_variable: plain map lookup on the closed-over execution_context.variables, applying LuaNumberMarshalling.to_lua/1, returning nil for an unset key or malformed argument. get_instance_state: enforce the self-instance-only restriction EXACTLY as the design specifies (script-supplied instance_id must equal execution_context.instance_id; anything else is :forbidden with NO Repo lookup attempted; only on a match does a Repo.get/3 with execution_context.prefix run, per the Letflow.Instances.get_by_id/2 pattern) -- this is the security-critical part SECURITY-REVIEWER will scrutinize hardest, implement it exactly as designed, do not take a shortcut. log: emit via Logger.log/3 (or equivalent), tagging every entry with script_identity/instance_id/trace_id sourced ONLY from execution_context, never from script arguments even as a fallback. Write real functional tests per the design's test-suite section and test/specs/REQ-159.md, including: read_variable returns the current value (with a round-tripped integer AND float proving REQ-150's rule is genuinely applied, not just referenced) and nil for unset; log emits a structured entry with all three correlation fields individually asserted; get_instance_state returns state for the script's own valid instance, and returns the SAME :forbidden result for both a real same-tenant sibling instance and a nonexistent id (proving indistinguishability); capability-denial test for each of the 3 functions (variable:read, instance:read, audit:log absent); no Letflow.Repo call anywhere in this diff uses a prefix derived from script-supplied input (a source-level test asserting this, similar to REQ-157's INV-CAP-1 structural guard, is worth adding if the design doesn't already specify one -- check). Follow the standard Step 2a procedure: verify branch, implement, mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix format --check-formatted, self-review checklist. Given this run's own design history (1 rework for a real authorization gap), be extra careful implementing get_instance_state's restriction precisely as designed. Run scripts/test_parallel.sh at least twice before reporting PASS. No migrations needed.
acceptance_criteria: read_variable round-trips both an integer and a float, asserting REQ-150's number-marshalling rule is genuinely applied (identity), not merely referenced
log emits a structured entry with script identity, instance ID, and trace ID all individually asserted
get_instance_state returns state for the script's own valid instance
get_instance_state returns the IDENTICAL :forbidden result for a real same-tenant sibling instance AND a nonexistent instance id -- proving no information leak distinguishing the two
A capability-denial test exists for each of the 3 functions (variable:read, instance:read, audit:log)
No Letflow.Repo call anywhere in this diff uses a prefix derived from script-supplied input -- verified by a test or explicit code review, not just asserted
At least 2 scripts/test_parallel.sh full-suite runs quoted, not just one file's tests

result.notes:
Implemented lib/letflow/design/req159-lua-host-api-read.md in full. New Letflow.Engine.LuaNumberMarshalling (to_lua/1, from_lua/1, both identity for integer/float/nil, pass-through otherwise, per REQ-150 Section 3). Extended Letflow.Engine.Lua.Platform: added execution_context type (%{instance_id, prefix, trace_id, script_identity, variables}), empty_execution_context/0 sentinel, new install/3, install/1 and install/2 now delegate down to install/3 with the empty sentinel (source-compatible, confirmed Sandbox.new/1's own call site at sandbox.ex:273 still calls Platform.install/1 unedited and still compiles). Replaced the read_variable/get_instance_state/log stub rows with real implementations per design Sections 4/5/6; write_variable/call_service/emit_event/now/fail and all required_capability values are untouched (matrix diff is stub-tag-only for the 3 rows, confirmed by a regression test).

get_instance_state implements the self-instance-only restriction EXACTLY as designed (Section 5): the script-supplied instance_id is checked for equality against execution_context.instance_id BEFORE any Repo call; any non-matching value (real same-tenant sibling OR nonexistent id) returns the identical {nil, %{reason: "forbidden"}} with NO Repo.get/3 attempted for that id -- proven by an explicit test that runs both cases and asserts the returned values are equal, not just each independently 'forbidden'. Only a match reaches Repo.get(InstanceProjection, instance_id, prefix: execution_context.prefix) -- prefix is never derived from the Lua-call argument, verified by a structural source-text test asserting platform.ex contains exactly one Repo.get( call site and that it reads 'Repo.get(InstanceProjection, instance_id, prefix: prefix)' with prefix bound only from execution_context.prefix.

TWO deviations from the design's literal text, both necessary (design text does not compile/run against the real tv-labs/lua dependency) and both flagged in platform.ex's own moduledoc for REVIEWER: (1) design Section 7.3's literal run_stub/4 (with an arity-1 Lua.set!/3 wrapper) cannot build get_instance_state's success-case Lua table -- tv-labs/lua requires Lua.encode!/2 against the current call's own Lua.t()/state to produce any dynamically-built table (confirmed directly against deps/lua/lib/lua.ex; a bare Elixir map returned from a Lua.set!/3 callback raises 'maps must be explicitly encoded to tables using Lua.encode!/2'). Fixed by using the library's own documented arity-2 wrapper form (fn args, lua -> ... end) and widening run_stub/3 to run_stub/5 (three prior args + execution_context + the call's Lua.t()) instead of run_stub/4. All other structural invariants the design cares about (one fold, one Lua.set!/3 call site per row, capabilities and execution_context both closed over once, the 5 unaffected rows unedited beyond ignoring the extra argument) are preserved exactly. (2) design Section 6.1 step 1's claim that a Lua-table argument (log's context) 'is already converted to an Elixir term by tv-labs/lua's own argument-marshalling at the call boundary' does not hold -- confirmed against deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/value.ex, an un-decoded table argument is still its internal {:tref, id} reference until Lua.decode!/2 is called explicitly. do_log/3 now calls Lua.decode!/2 on context before it reaches Logger.log/3's metadata.

Test suite (test/letflow/engine/lua/platform_test.exs, extended; test/letflow/engine/lua_number_marshalling_test.exs, new) covers every acceptance criterion: read_variable round-trips an integer (3) and a float (3.0) through math.type() assertions proving REQ-150 identity is genuinely applied, plus unset-key and malformed-argument cases; log's 3 correlation fields are asserted individually via ExUnit.CaptureLog with :metadata formatter opts (real Postgres-free), plus a raw :logger handler test for the non-scalar context field (the default text formatter silently drops map metadata -- confirmed and documented); get_instance_state has a real-Postgres test (TenantProvisioning-provisioned tenant schema, mirroring test/letflow/event_store_test.exs's own fixture idiom) proving self-instance success, invalid_id/forbidden/not_found/no_execution_context structured errors in the exact Section 5.2 step order, and the security-critical identical-forbidden-for-sibling-vs-nonexistent test; capability-denial tests for all 3 functions; matrix/stub-tag regression guards; install/1 and install/2 backward-compatibility tests; and the structural no-script-supplied-prefix guard described above.
